output.answer: Yes. The most recent company-specific report I found says GM announced plans to lay off 361 workers at two Lansing, Michigan, plants, effective January 17, 2027, as the facilities undergo retooling; GM expects to recall employees after the changeover. Separately, GM temporarily laid off 1,300 Factory ZERO workers in March 2026 while production was adjusted to EV demand.
caveats: The Lansing figure is reported as 361 by mlive.com, while CBS Detroit reported 350 workers and a January 14, 2027 layoff date for the same two sites; the reports appear to reflect differing WARN-notice details.

The Lansing layoffs are described as tied to retooling with expected recall, while the Factory ZERO action was explicitly temporary; these figures should not be treated as a permanent company-wide headcount reduction.

passages.quote: General Motors has announced plans to lay off 361 workers employed at assembly and stamping plants in Lansing.
The facilities will be retooled for future production, including the Cadillac CT5... GM expects to call back employees after the changeover
“Factory ZERO will temporarily adjust production to align EV production with market demand,” a GM spokesperson said. The temporary layoff affects 1,300 workers.

output.question: Has General Motors announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: GM announced plans to lay off 361 workers at the Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping plants, effective January 17, 2027.
GM said the Lansing facilities would be retooled for future production and expected to call back affected employees after the changeover.
GM temporarily laid off 1,300 workers at its Detroit Factory ZERO EV plant while idling the plant to align production with market demand.
